claims: Same car, same 7.5 cm bump height; a 0.9 m bump gives a higher peak body acceleration than a 3.7 m hump at 10, 20 and 30 km/h in a simple quarter-car simulation with assumed car values (not calibrated, not a safety statement).
frame_plan_note: frames 1-640 = three slow-motion passes (A 20 km/h 1-320, B 30 km/h 321-480, C 10 km/h 481-640), 641-960 = peak-acceleration comparison card
